source.title: Exclusive Unlearning
source.authors: Mutsumi Sasaki; Kouta Nakayama; Yusuke Miyao; Yohei Oseki; Masaru Isonuma

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports a fine-tuning recovery result and jailbreak evaluations after its unlearning method, including an explicit conclusion that subsequent fine-tuning can restore harmful behavior. This refines the claim: the method resisted tested jailbreaks but was vulnerable to later fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports target-domain retention and general-benchmark results, but these do not measure recovery attacks or targeted harmful-knowledge accuracy. The jailbreak ASR rows below record the prompting-only attack outcomes. No ablation, quantization, or recovery-by-rephrasing-only experiment is reported.
record.test_reason: The study proposes a new unlearning method (EU) and tests it against unseen jailbreak prompts (E, F) and against later fine-tuning on 400 Alpaca examples (B, F). It also reports jailbreak ASR for a conventional gradient-ascent unlearning baseline (E). Its result restates F: EU resists the tested jailbreaks, but the authors say its forgetting is 'not robust to subsequent fine-tuning'. The measure is harmful-output ASR from a ShieldLM judge, not accuracy on forgotten knowledge.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that EU keeps target-domain capability while cutting harmful and unseen-jailbreak ASR to near zero, outperforming DPO, enumerative Unlearning, Eraser and SKU. They also note two limits. Fine-tuning on 400 Alpaca examples raises ASR to about 40%, suggesting suppression rather than erasure, so EU suits settings without later fine-tuning. EU also degrades capabilities outside the retained domain.
record.recipe_differences: EU combines a self-generated-text entropy/uniformity objective with fine-tuning on a specified retention domain; the recovery experiment applies later Alpaca fine-tuning. This is not the original claim’s specified unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, retention domain, and jailbreak set. The reported vulnerability also depends on subsequent fine-tuning; the tested fine-tune checkpoint and exact baseline ASR are not specified.

fits_no_version.finding: In t-SNE of final-layer last-token states, jailbreak prompts shift harmful inputs toward the general-domain region under conventional unlearning, so they escape forgetting; under EU they do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak recovery after enumerative unlearning arises because jailbreaks move harmful-input representations out of the forgotten region.

record.problems: The fine-tuning recovery result is described only for an unspecified EU checkpoint and gives an approximate ASR without the exact pre-fine-tuning value or attack-set details. ASR is a safety-behavior measure, not direct accuracy on the forgotten knowledge. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports jailbreak ASRs for Eraser and SKU in Tables 1 and 9; those comparative baseline rows are not included here. EU and conventional Unlearning rows were retained to capture the proposed method and the direct enumerative-unlearning comparison.

untested.parts: No accuracy on targeted knowledge (e.g., WMDP-style) is measured. ASR is a judged harmful-output rate. General ability drops substantially outside the retained domain (Table 3).

Only an unrelated relearning set (400 Alpaca examples) is tested, on one unspecified EU checkpoint. Loosely related sets and subsets of the forgotten data are not tested. No baseline unlearning method is fine-tuned.
No activation-direction ablation. The t-SNE analysis is descriptive and does not test recovery.
Only template jailbreaks (20 prompts in six categories) are tested. Other languages and in-context information are not tested.
EU is not tested against quantization or internal-edit attacks.

missing.what: Harm-1/Harm-2 ASR for the Unlearning baseline (0.0 in nearly all settings). This is the pre-attack baseline against which jailbreak recovery (E) should be read.
Self-generation sensitivity: JB ASR rises to 19.7/21.6 at temperature 0.7, 55.8/61.6 at top-k 0, and 33.0/39.9 at user length 16.
EU jailbreak ASR across λ values, e.g., OLMo-2-1B medical JB-1 7.5% at λ 0.2–0.4.
Exact pre/post fine-tuning ASR, attack set and checkpoint for the Alpaca relearning result (not reported by the paper).

record.verdict_notes: The math-domain Unlearning rows (R26–R33) were read from the DPO line of Table 9 and are corrected above. EU's 'forgetting' is partly a decoding-time filter: outputs close to uniform are replaced with a fixed refusal (threshold Δ=5; Table 8 shows threshold insensitivity). Its low ASR therefore reflects gibberish-plus-refusal rather than verified knowledge deletion. ASR is judged by ShieldLM-14B, and no uncertainty is reported. The study is not among the original sources.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance together with simple attacks failing to recover it.
Tests further fine-tuning on 400 Alpaca examples only; the paper does not specify the tested checkpoint or provide an exact pre-fine-tuning ASR value.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit experiment. The authors’ suppression interpretation follows from the fine-tuning result, not a separate internal-mechanism analysis.
Tests jailbreak prompts on harmful questions; does not test prompt rephrasing alone, other languages, or in-context information as recovery attacks.
Tests the proposed method against jailbreak inputs and subsequent fine-tuning, but not against quantization, internal edits, or the other prompting variants named in the claim.
